notes: The two failures differ in weight: the lint failure is large (76 findings, mostly semicolons and clause-joining dashes), so it genuinely discriminates old skill from new; the behavioral failure hangs on one item (TKT-005 naming `due_at`/`created_at`) out of 40, and the all-or-nothing wording means one slip zeroes the assertion, so consider a per-item count or threshold. The 'written before any docs/ file' ordering rests on an executor-authored transcript summary, not a tool log, so it is attestation rather than evidence; file mtimes or the harness log would make it checkable. Two outcomes no assertion covers: (a) the executor surfaced two genuine code/spec conflicts (unknown priority escaping as a traceback with exit 1; KeyError on replay of an orphan event), exactly what the skill wants, and earns no credit for it; (b) self-reported verification is unreliable: the proposal's conflicts section cites 'CLI-006' for the TODO that lives on CLI-008, and the executor's verification step claimed 'no function/class/file names in spec bodies' while `due_at` was present. The placeholder assertion passes but by-eye grading could false-fail it on legitimate `<id>` output markers; check_run.py handles the distinction. No user_notes.md or metrics.json were produced.
